content.title: St. Patrick's Day Parade, Chicago River dyeing: What to know for annual celebration
content.text: Editor's note: The video in the player above is from the dyeing of the Chicago River in 2025. St. Patrick's Day celebrations are coming up and Chicago, home to one of the largest Irish-American populations in the U.S., is widely known for its festivities. From the iconic dyeing of the Chicago River to the popular St. Patrick's Day parade, Chicago goes big for the annual holiday. In fact, the city's South Side Irish Parade is the largest community-based St. Patrick's Day Parade outside of Dublin, Ireland. So what should you know and when are the events happening? When is St. Patrick's Day? For 2026, St. Patrick's Day falls on Tuesday, March 17. That's not the day that many of the city's festivities will happen, however. Local When is the Chicago River dyeing? The dyeing of the Chicago River will mark one of the first celebrations to kick off the series of events. The annual dyeing of the water begins on Saturday, March 14. What time is the river dye? While the river dye typically gets underway away at around 10 a.m., the process typically takes around 45 minutes to an hour, and the amount of time can depend on conditions. During the river dyeing, members of the Chicago Plumbers Union - situated in boats - use a concoction that sprays dye out of plumping pipes and spout pumps, turning the water a green hue. The mysterious mixture actually comes out orange, but the color changes to green once the dye sets in. The impeccable brilliant green only lasts for a few hours, with Choose Chicago explaining the water will retain a shade of green after the initial dyeing, but it will slowly fade over time. When is the Chicago St. Patrick’s Day Parade? Also on Saturday, March 14, is the Chicago St. Patrick's Day Parade. The parade will feature bagpipers, dancers, green floats and more traveling down Columbus Drive. The theme of this year's parade is Faith, Peace and Unity. What about the South Side Irish Parade? A family-friendly tradition for more than 40 years and counting, the South Side Irish Parade will take place on Sunday, March 15. As in past years, it will begin at noon from West 103rd Street and Western Avenue in Chicago’s Beverly/Morgan Park neighborhood. And the Northwest Side Irish Parade? Festivities also stretch to other parts of the city. The Northwest Side Irish Parade, billed as a celebration of faith, family and heritage, also steps off at noon on Sunday. The route begins at North Neola Avenue and West Raven Street then proceeds along North Northwest Highway before ending at Harlem Avenue.
